input.summary: This proposal preserves a precisely bounded, single-configuration descriptive pilot using the emulated-netem-v1 runner. One cubic flow (1 MB, 10 ms delay, 100 Mbit/s bottleneck, 125 KB buffer) is executed once to record flow_completion_time_ms. The result is compared only with a subsequently identified matched baseline under exact absolute tolerance. The wider paper claim — that adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions — remains unresolved by this pilot. No population inference, causal conclusion, or monetary charge is asserted. The protocol is reproduced exactly from the packet with source hashes retained as supplied.
questions: What matched baseline configuration (e.g., cubic flow at 30 ms delay) will be used for the subsequent comparison, and has its execution specification been frozen?

Is the script identifier 'netem_cubic_benchmark_nines.py' confirmed as the correct entry point for the emulated-netem-v1 runner, or should it be 'netem_nines.py' as referenced in the runner documentation?
Are there any additional replications planned beyond this single pilot run before the broader 20 ms delay comparison is attempted?

proposal.problem: Check a precisely bounded compression hypothesis before any larger workload study. This pilot executes one frozen netem specification for a single cubic flow and records completion time for later matched comparison only.
proposal.question: What is the completion time of this one frozen cubic flow (1 MB, cubic CCA, 10 ms delay, 100 Mbit/s bottleneck, 125 KB buffer)?
proposal.hypothesis: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time.
proposal.conditions: One 1 MB cubic flow with 10 ms delay, 100 Mbit/s bottleneck and 125 KB buffer; a descriptive implementation pilot. Decompression must recover the exact byte hash of the original payload. Encoded bytes include gzip framing.
proposal.related_work: Novelty is not claimed. No literature search or full review is asserted. Existing stdlib algorithms are used. The wider paper claim remains unresolved pending a matched baseline run.
proposal.alternatives: Any reduction may reflect repetitive input; real-world benefit requires separate representative workloads and timing controls. A failed or missing completion time remains failed or missing. This one configuration does not resolve the broad delay comparison.
proposal.design: Execute the one frozen netem specification (cubic-10ms), record flow_completion_time_ms, and compare only with a subsequently identified matched baseline configuration. No population inference is drawn from this single pilot run.
proposal.metrics: flow_completion_time_ms in ms; no published numeric target is available. Exact absolute difference tolerance of 0 applies only to matched numeric comparisons against a separately supplied baseline.
proposal.controls: Same original payload for both configurations; decompression must recover its exact byte hash; count encoded bytes including the gzip framing. Exact observation/configuration/metric/units matching enforced. No zero imputation. Unique observation keys required.
proposal.falsification: A failed or missing completion time remains failed or missing. This one configuration does not resolve the broad delay comparison. Stop on any input identity, schema, configuration, units or budget violation; preserve the failed attempt. Unmatched observations are excluded and recorded; duplicates, unit mismatches and changed inputs fail the run.
